profiles.meeting_scenario: A state-level emergency management office and a regional healthcare coalition are holding a coordination meeting to align their workstreams before a coastal hurricane tabletop exercise and a follow-on governance briefing on how the region's response network has evolved under the NRF model. The immediate context is that both teams are contributing to a shared interagency package: a network map of participating organizations, a county contact matrix, and a short readiness summary for senior officials. The agenda is to confirm which version of the network artifacts each side is using, align handoffs for the county contact list, and agree on what will be considered 'ready' for Friday's exercise support deadline. The expected outcome is apparent agreement on who will send the updated map, who will complete the county contact matrix, and what materials will be circulated by the end of the week.

members.name: Dana Ruiz
members.role: State Emergency Management Interagency Planning Lead
members.expertise: Emergency operations planning, ESF coordination, interagency governance, WebEOC workflows
members.background: Dana works in the state emergency management agency and manages cross-sector planning products used by the state EOC, including organizational relationship maps and resource coordination templates for multi-county incidents.
members.private_state: Dana wants the exercise package to be operationally usable inside the state EOC with minimal rework, and is trying to avoid a last-minute scramble to reconcile partner lists across agencies.
hidden_assumptions: When partners say a network artifact is 'validated,' they mean each organization's current liaison or duty desk has confirmed participation details for this operational cycle.
The 'latest network map' refers to the June 12 SharePoint version that includes dependency lines and ESF tagging, because that is the version tied to current planning documents.
A 'county contact' deliverable naturally includes all county-level operational interfaces needed in incident coordination, not just the health and medical lane.
If a package is 'ready for Friday,' it is ready to be loaded into WebEOC and used by planners even if minor formatting or logo issues remain.

members.name: Leah Morgan
members.expertise: Hospital coalition coordination, medical surge planning, partner engagement, briefing preparation
members.background: Leah supports a multi-county healthcare coalition that coordinates hospitals, EMS, public health departments, and long-term care partners during disasters, and she often turns planning inputs into shareable partner briefings.
members.private_state: Leah wants to provide a polished, partner-safe package to coalition members and protect her team's limited bandwidth by keeping the deliverable within the medical coordination scope they already maintain.
hidden_assumptions: When people say a partner set is 'validated,' they usually mean the organization is already covered by an active participation agreement or annual coalition roster, so fresh contact confirmation is optional.
The 'network map from last month' is the June 3 workshop slide version that was already socialized with coalition members and is therefore the practical baseline.
A request for 'county-level contacts' in this context is shorthand for the ESF-8 and healthcare coordination contacts her coalition routinely manages.
If materials are 'ready for Friday,' they should be externally shareable to coalition members as a clean PDF or slide appendix without obvious placeholders or internal annotations.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as a 'validated' partner list
misalignment_points.surface_form: They both refer to using the 'validated partner list' for the exercise package.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means a list whose entries were actively confirmed this cycle by current liaisons or duty desks.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means a list of organizations already covered by standing coalition participation agreements or annual rosters, even if individual contacts were not recently reconfirmed.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both meanings sound professionally reasonable and use the same reassuring term, so each hears the other as simply endorsing standard due diligence rather than signaling a different threshold.

misalignment_points.topic: Which 'network map from last month' is the baseline
misalignment_points.surface_form: They discuss updating 'the network map from last month' before circulation.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is referring to the June 12 SharePoint map revised after the state planning call, with ESF tags and dependency links added.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is referring to the June 3 workshop slide map emailed after the regional planning workshop, which coalition members have already seen.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both artifacts were produced in the same month, both are legitimately called the network map, and neither participant expects that the other is anchored to a different file because the phrase feels uniquely identifying in context.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that Leah will finish the 'county-level contacts' section.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 expects the section to cover the full county interface set needed for coordination: EOC, public health, EMS, sheriff, public works, and school transportation where relevant.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes the section is limited to the healthcare coalition's usual county-facing contacts: public health, hospital duty officers, EMS, and medical coordination points.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Because Leah already owns a county contact spreadsheet for her coalition, Dana naturally assumes it can be extended without saying so, while Leah hears the request as a normal handoff of her existing scope.

misalignment_points.topic: What it means for the package to be 'ready for Friday'
misalignment_points.surface_form: They align on having the materials 'ready for Friday.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the package is operationally usable by Friday morning for internal EOC exercise support, with rough formatting acceptable if the fields are populated.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the package is finished enough by end of day Friday to circulate externally to coalition partners, which requires cleaner formatting and removal of placeholders.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: A Friday target sounds specific enough to create false confidence, but each person silently applies the standard from their own downstream use case—operational deployment versus partner-facing distribution.

For me, ready for Friday means planners can use it Friday morning in WebEOC support, even if a few cosmetic edits come later.
